About this summary

Built from the RRCS results on this page: the contact pairs whose |ΔRRCS| is at or above this receptor's threshold, grouped by the segment of each residue (a pair between two segments counts for both). The bars show the sum of ΔRRCS in each direction, scaled to the largest segment; the number is how many such pairs touch the segment. Open a segment to see its largest changes. Choosing a pair marks it on the snake plot, in the tables, in the charts and in the 3D view.

The one-line answer and the "Largest changes" list cover the helices TM1 to TM7 and H8, where the models are best constrained. 3 of the 8 largest changes overall involve a loop or a terminus; "Include loops and termini" lists them, marked loop or tail. Treat those with more caution.

Segment order: "Helices first" lists TM1 to TM7 and H8 together, then the loops, then the termini. "Sequence" follows the chain from the N-terminus. The models are most reliable in the helices. The choice applies to every segment list and chart on the site and in the Studio, and is remembered in this browser.

For an explanation of the scores and colors, see Understanding the results.

Interactive snake plot

Each circle is one residue, laid out as in GPCRdb. The buttons recolor the residues by a data layer. The arcs are the contact pairs at or above this receptor's threshold, within the selected filters; open a loop to show its contacts. Hover a residue to see its partners, click it to select it across the page, and click an ICL or ECL label to open or close that loop.

Red: stronger in the active model. Blue: stronger in the inactive model.

Transmembrane domain analysis

A residue is listed when its largest single contact change or the sum of its signed contact changes reaches this receptor's threshold (|ΔRRCS| ≥ 2.52). The column follows the signed sum: positive is stronger overall in the active model, negative stronger overall in the inactive model. "Largest single contact" changes the value shown, not the column. The threshold formula is in Methods.

Methods

RRCS analysis. Residue-Residue Contact Scores (RRCS) quantify pairwise residue contact strength from inter-atomic distances; comparing active and inactive structures predicted by AlphaFold multistate (Heo L, Feig M. Proteins 2022;90(11):1873-1885, doi 10.1002/prot.26382) or, for some states, plain AlphaFold2 (Jumper J et al. Nature 2021;596:583-589, doi 10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2) gives a per-pair ΔRRCS. The models are GPCRdb's 2024-05-15 build; across the 283 receptors, plain AlphaFold2 built 165 inactive and 26 active models.

Receptor-specific ΔRRCS threshold. |ΔRRCS| ≥ 2.52, computed as max(mean(|Δ|) + σ, 0.2). The threshold is never lower than 0.2. Contact pairs with |ΔRRCS| below 0.2 do not pass this rule.

Variant data. Population frequencies from gnomAD v4.1.2 (dataset gnomad_r4, accessed 18 October 2026) (Chen et al., Nature 2024, doi 10.1038/s41586-023-06045-0); pathogenicity predictions from AlphaMissense (Cheng et al., Science 2023; predictions copyright 2023 DeepMind Technologies Limited, CC BY 4.0); conservation from VarSite scores served by ProtVar (Stephenson et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2024, doi 10.1093/nar/gkae413). The Het count column shows heterozygote allele counts (allele count minus twice the homozygote count); homozygote counts are not shown.

Structural annotation. TM domain boundaries and generic numbering from GPCRdb (Herrera et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2025, doi 10.1093/nar/gkae1065); protein accessions from UniProt (The UniProt Consortium, Nucleic Acids Res 2025, doi 10.1093/nar/gkae1010).

What is RRCS?

Residue-Residue Contact Score (RRCS) measures how strongly two amino acids interact in a protein structure. Here, ΔRRCS compares contact scores in the active and inactive receptor models.

ΔRRCS (Delta RRCS) shows the difference in contact strength between states:

  • Positive ΔRRCS. Contact is stronger in the active state.
  • Negative ΔRRCS. Contact is stronger in the inactive state.
  • Large |ΔRRCS|. Notable contact-score difference between the active and inactive models.

Residues with large ΔRRCS values mark positions whose contact environment differs between the active and inactive models. These positions may be useful candidates for structural interpretation or follow-up variant analysis, but they should not be interpreted as functional proof on their own.

Pathogenicity predictions

AlphaMissense scores estimate the likelihood that a missense substitution disrupts function, based on structural and evolutionary features. The published score thresholds bin each variant as:

  • Likely pathogenic: score > 0.564.
  • Ambiguous: 0.34 ≤ score ≤ 0.564.
  • Likely benign: score < 0.34.

Classes follow the source predictions before display rounding.

Conservation & population data

Conservation score. How well-preserved a position is across species (0 = variable, 1 = conserved). Highly conserved positions are often functionally important, but conservation alone is not proof of function.

Allele frequency. Population frequency of the variant in gnomAD v4.1.2 (dataset gnomad_r4, accessed 18 October 2026). Rare variants are common across the genome and many are undersampled; rarity alone is not evidence of pathogenicity.
